name: Job’s three friends
charge: Speaking of God the thing that is not right; condemning the righteous, having found no answer
summary: Eliphaz the Temanite, Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite came from their own places by appointment to mourn with Job and comfort him, and sat with him on the ground seven days and seven nights without a word. Then they reasoned from his suffering back to his guilt, and Eliphaz at last invented the sins outright. The Lord answered them by name: they had not spoken of him the thing that was right, as his servant Job had, and he sent them with sacrifice to the man they had condemned, that he might pray for them.
offenseFull: When Job’s three friends heard of all the evil that had come on him, each came from his own place by appointment to mourn with him and to comfort him. They lifted up their voice and wept, rent every man his mantle, sprinkled dust on their heads toward heaven, and sat down with him on the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spoke a word, for they saw that his grief was very great (Job 2:11-13). Friends who come to a man’s affliction with correction and hard truth are not the fault here. What is wanted is people who give straight facts and not people who butter a man up while he is in the wrong. The fault is the conclusion they reached and would not abandon.

Eliphaz began where it cuts deepest: Job had instructed many, strengthened the weak hands, upheld him that was falling and strengthened the feeble knees, and now that it had come on him, he fainted (Job 4:3-5). There is one that is wise and teaches many and yet is unprofitable to himself (Ecclesiasticus 37:19): you were the man who comforted everybody, and now your own turn has come and you want to give up. That much was fair warning. Then he went further and asked who ever perished being innocent, or where the righteous were cut off (Job 4:7), which turns every affliction into proof of sin. Bildad asked whether God perverts judgment, pointed at Job’s dead children as cast away for their transgression, and promised a latter end that would greatly increase if Job were pure and upright, on the false premise that he was not already upright (Job 8:3-7; Job 1:1, 5). Zophar told him God exacted of him less than his iniquity deserved (Job 11:6). Then Eliphaz stopped inferring and began inventing: he said Job’s wickedness was great, that he had taken a pledge from his brother for nothing and stripped the naked of their clothing and withheld bread from the hungry (Job 22:5-7), none of which the record supports. Job named it while it was being done: they were forgers of lies and physicians of no value and miserable comforters, and he asked whether they would speak wickedly for God and talk deceitfully for him (Job 13:4, 7; Job 16:2). Defending God with false accusations against his servant is the thing this case is entered for. Elihu’s wrath was kindled against the three because they had found no answer and yet had condemned Job (Job 32:3); and it was Elihu who spoke the word that reaches to our own day, that by reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry, and they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty (Job 35:9).
judgmentFull: The Lord told Eliphaz the Temanite that his wrath was kindled against him and against his two friends, because they had not spoken of him the thing that was right, as his servant Job had (Job 42:7). The remedy was sacrifice and intercession, and it had to be carried to the man they had accused: seven bullocks and seven rams, brought to his servant Job, a burnt offering offered for themselves, and Job would pray for them, for the Lord would accept him, or else he would deal with them after their folly (Job 42:8). That is how the priesthood always worked in Israel: the sacrifice is brought to the righteous one and offered on the sinner’s behalf, and the man who does not bring it is not forgiven.

The three who had argued so long for Job’s guilt now depended on the prayer of the man they had condemned, and the effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man avails much (James 5:16). It was not the prayer by itself, but the prayer of a righteous man; the Most High deals with those who are dealing in righteousness. They did as the Lord commanded them, and the Lord also accepted Job; and it was in the praying for these friends that his own captivity was turned (Job 42:9-10). Afterward his brethren and sisters and former acquaintances came and ate bread with him and comforted him, every man bringing him a piece of money and an earring of gold (Job 42:11). The friends were restored along with everything else.

lawsResolved.text: Doing injustice by justifying the wicked and condemning the righteous is an abomination and condemned by God.
We should not speak evil of someone out of suspicions or assumptions.
You shall not lie to one another.
Do not be a witness against your neighbor without cause.

text.text: Now when Job’s three friends heard of all this evil that was come upon him, they came every one from his own place; Eliphaz the Temanite, and Bildad the Shuhite, and Zophar the Naamathite: for they had made an appointment together to come to mourn with him and to comfort him.
And when they lifted up their eyes afar off, and knew him not, they lifted up their voice, and wept; and they rent every one his mantle, and sprinkled dust upon their heads toward heaven.
So they sat down with him upon the ground seven days and seven nights, and none spake a word unto him: for they saw that his grief was very great.
Behold, thou hast instructed many, and thou hast strengthened the weak hands.
Thy words have upholden him that was falling, and thou hast strengthened the feeble knees.
But now it is come upon thee, and thou faintest; it toucheth thee, and thou art troubled.
There is one that is wise and teacheth many, and yet is unprofitable to himself.
Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?
Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?
If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;
If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;
If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
Though thy beginning was small, yet thy latter end should greatly increase.
There was a man in the land of Uz, whose name was Job; and that man was perfect and upright, and one that feared God, and eschewed evil.

And it was so, when the days of their feasting were gone about, that Job sent and sanctified them, and rose up early in the morning, and offered burnt offerings according to the number of them all: for Job said, It may be that my sons have sinned, and cursed God in their hearts. Thus did Job continually.
And that he would shew thee the secrets of wisdom, that they are double to that which is! Know therefore that God exacteth of thee less than thine iniquity deserveth.
Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?
For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
Thou hast not given water to the weary to drink, and thou hast withholden bread from the hungry.
But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.
Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him?
I have heard many such things: miserable comforters are ye all.
Also against his three friends was his wrath kindled, because they had found no answer, and yet had condemned Job.
By reason of the multitude of oppressions they make the oppressed to cry: they cry out by reason of the arm of the mighty.

And it was so, that after the Lord had spoken these words unto Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.

Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.
Confess your faults one to another, and pray one for another, that ye may be healed. The effectual fervent prayer of a righteous man availeth much.
So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the Lord commanded them: the Lord also accepted Job.
And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.

Then came there unto him all his brethren, and all his sisters, and all they that had been of his acquaintance before, and did eat bread with him in his house: and they bemoaned him, and comforted him over all the evil that the Lord had brought upon him: every man also gave him a piece of money, and every one an earring of gold.
Remember, I pray thee, who ever perished, being innocent? or where were the righteous cut off?
Even as I have seen, they that plow iniquity, and sow wickedness, reap the same.
Doth God pervert judgment? or doth the Almighty pervert justice?
If thy children have sinned against him, and he have cast them away for their transgression;
If thou wouldest seek unto God betimes, and make thy supplication to the Almighty;
If thou wert pure and upright; surely now he would awake for thee, and make the habitation of thy righteousness prosperous.
Is not thy wickedness great? and thine iniquities infinite?
For thou hast taken a pledge from thy brother for nought, and stripped the naked of their clothing.
But ye are forgers of lies, ye are all physicians of no value.
O that ye would altogether hold your peace! and it should be your wisdom.
Hear now my reasoning, and hearken to the pleadings of my lips.
Will ye speak wickedly for God? and talk deceitfully for him?

And it was so, that after the Lord had spoken these words unto Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz the Temanite, My wrath is kindled against thee, and against thy two friends: for ye have not spoken of me the thing that is right, as my servant Job hath.

Therefore take unto you now seven bullocks and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and offer up for yourselves a burnt offering; and my servant Job shall pray for you: for him will I accept: lest I deal with you after your folly, in that ye have not spoken of me the thing which is right, like my servant Job.
So Eliphaz the Temanite and Bildad the Shuhite and Zophar the Naamathite went, and did according as the Lord commanded them: the Lord also accepted Job.
And the Lord turned the captivity of Job, when he prayed for his friends: also the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.
